paper.code_data_availability: “Data were processed and analyzed via Statistics Denmark’s servers and therefore cannot be shared.” (section 3, p. …

registers.name_in_paper: the Danish administrative registers (provided by Statistics Denmark)
registers.role: controls / covariates and sample frame for the full population of Danish households

registers.name_in_paper: information on PVs from Energinet.dk (the Danish transmission system operator)
registers.role: treatment / outcome (PVs ownership, net settlement scheme) and sample frame for PVs owners
variables_mentioned: anonymized personal identification code of the registrant
date of registration (not date of installation)

registers.name_in_paper: 2018 questionnaire survey of Danish PVs owners, carried out by Statistics Denmark on behalf of Aalborg University
registers.role: outcomes for the second part of the analysis (inspiration and motivation for buying PVs)
variables_mentioned: Were you involved in the decision on buying PVs?
Were the PVs bought in combination with…?
Did you know others with PVs prior to buying PVs yourself?
Did you do any of the following related to PVs prior to buying?
How important were the following reasons for your purchase of PVs? (11 statements)

linkages: Data were merged using unique address codes linked to unique personal identification codes, both of which were anonymized
Using an anonymized address code, the register data were merged with information on PVs from Energinet.dk
Survey respondents (a stratified random sample of 4567 PVs owners drawn from a full population of 72,967 Danish PVs households) linked to the administrative data
Data were processed and analyzed via Statistics Denmark’s servers

sample.universe: The full population of Danish household PVs owner addresses registered with Energinet.dk (73,974 PVs households as of 2015) together with the full population of Danish households, plus a 2018 questionnaire survey of 2505 PVs owners
sample.unit_of_observation: household-year for the register panel analysis (Table 1); PVs-owner household for Table 2; individual survey respondent for Figures 2-7
selection_rules: Register panel covers the years 2000, 2005 and 2007-2015
PVs owner addresses are those registered as PVs owners with Energinet.dk, observed through 2015
Early adopters: bought PVs on or before November 19, 2012 (installation may have occurred later) and on annual net metering scheme
Later adopters: bought PVs after November 19, 2012 and until the end of 2015, and on hourly or real-time net metering scheme
Before combining with other data, early adopters included 72,967 households and later adopters 3699 households
Survey: stratified random selection of 4567 individual PVs owners from a full population of 72,967 Danish PVs households
Survey: respondents sampled to ensure an equal distribution of annually metered and other metering schemes (hourly and real time)
Survey: intentionally targeted at an equal number of men and women; where a household consisted of a couple, one of them was chosen at random
Survey: 2505 people responded via a web link, a response rate of 54.9%
Survey analyses drop respondents who did not take part in the purchasing decision, non-responses, ‘Do not know’ responses and observations with missing information in the administrative data
sample.period: Register panel 2000, 2005 and 2007-2015; survey fielded in the fall of 2018
sample.n_observations: 13,878,571 household-year observations (Table 1); 73,557 PVs-owner households (Table 2); 2505 survey respondents, with 2094 used in the factor analysis
sample.n_individuals: 1,574,675 households and 73,974 PVs households (Table 1); 72,967 early-adopter and 3699 later-adopter households before combining with other data

construction_notes: Buying PVs is a binary indicator of the household being registered as owner of a PV system in the given year; date of registration is observed, not date of installation
Household income enters as quintiles with Q3 as the reference category
Highest attained education in household has “Primary” as reference category
Average age of household has “40 or lower” as reference category
Location has “Large cities and suburbs” as reference category
Construction period has “before 1961” as reference category
Housing type has “Single-family” as reference category; heating form has “District heating” as reference category
Table 1 is estimated with the generalized estimating equation (GEE) / population-averaged approach, which adjusts the logistic coefficients and standard errors for autocorrelation across years
Exploratory factor analysis of 11 motivation statements used oblique promax rotation; Kendall’s tau was used to inspect associations beforehand because the items are ordinal
‘Don’t know’ responses were removed before the factor analysis, leaving four ordered response categories (1 “Not important at all”, 2 “Less important”, 3 “Important”, 4 “Very important”)

Three statements were dropped from the factor analysis: ‘We had some money that we wanted to invest’, ‘To increase the market value of the house’ (uniqueness higher than 0.7 and loadings below 0.35) and ‘To be more self-sufficient’ (loaded equally and below 0.33 on two factors)
The three factors were constructed into summative scales (responses simply added up) and normalized to a scale from 0 to 1; Cronbach’s Alpha coefficients were higher than 0.67
Differences in group means and proportions are tested with two-tailed two-sample t-tests

claims.statement: In a population-averaged logistic regression on the full Danish household panel, household income Q1 (lowest quintile), relative to Q3 is associated with a lower likelihood of buying PVs in a given year.

treatment.label: Household income Q1 (lowest quintile), relative to Q3

register_source.value: Danish administrative registers provided by Statistics Denmark (no register code or register variable name is given)

definition.value: Indicator for the household being in the 1st (lowest) quintile of household income; the 3rd quintile is the omitted reference category.

timing.value: Measured in the same panel year as the outcome (2000, 2005, 2007–2015)

outcome.label: Buying PVs

register_source.value: Energinet.dk (Danish transmission system operator): net settlement scheme, anonymized personal identification code of the registrant and date of registration

definition.value: Binary indicator equal to 1 if the household is registered as owner of a PV system in the given panel year and 0 otherwise; PVs registrations come from Energinet.dk and are linked to register households through an anonymized address code. Date of registration, not date of installation, is observed.

timing.value: Measured in each panel year (2000, 2005 and 2007–2015); the panel model compares households buying PVs with other households not buying PVs in that particular year.

estimand.target_population: Danish households (PVs-owner addresses and all other households) observed in 2000, 2005 and 2007–2015

population.description: Panel of the full population of PVs owner addresses registered with Energinet.dk through 2015 together with the full population of Danish households as comparison group
population.selection: Full population; no sample selection beyond the register coverage of Danish households and the Energinet.dk registry of PVs owner addresses

identification.source_of_variation: No exogenous variation is used: observational comparison of the full population of registered PVs owner households with all other Danish households across the panel years

key_assumptions.assumption: The coefficients are population-averaged associations between household characteristics and PVs purchase and are to be read as in a cross-sectional regression, not as causal effects
Serial dependence across panel years is handled by the GEE working correlation structure, which adjusts the logistic coefficients and the standard errors for autocorrelation
key_assumptions.supported_by: Szmaragd et al. (2013) cited; section 3.3.1 contrasts the GEE estimates with a pooled logistic regression that would not account for serial correlation

key_assumptions.assumption: The anonymized address code correctly links Energinet.dk PVs registrations to register households, so that a household counts as a PVs buyer in the year in which its PVs were registered; date of installation is not observed
Each characteristic is adjusted for the other household characteristics entered in the model; the paper does not discuss unobserved confounding or state an exogeneity condition

threats_discussed: Pooled logistic regression would not account for serial correlation across years
Only date of registration, not date of installation, is observed

estimator.value: Population-averaged logistic regression estimated by the GEE approach (multivariate weighted nonlinear least squares)

estimation.specification: Population-averaged (GEE) logistic regression of an indicator for buying PVs in a given year on household income quintile, highest attained education, technical education, average household age, presence of a young child and of a teenager, location, construction period, housing type and heating form. No estimating equation is printed.
controls: Average age of household (ref. “40 or lower”)
estimation.clustering: Not stated; the GEE approach adjusts the logistic coefficients and standard errors for autocorrelation across years within households

adjustment_set.label: Average age of household (ref. “40 or lower”)

heterogeneity.dimension: Early versus later adopters (net metering scheme)
heterogeneity.finding: Table 2 shows that among PVs owners only the 4th income quintile differs significantly from the reference quintile in the likelihood of being a later adopter.
